name: King Pedro
description: King Pedro is a variant of the popular American card game Pedro (also known as Cinch or 63), played primarily in the northeastern United States and Canada. It adds the King of trumps as an additional scoring card worth 5 points, making the total points available 19 per hand instead of the standard 14. It is a trick-taking game where the 5 of trumps (the Pedro) and the 5 of the same color (the Left Pedro) are the most valuable cards.

content.text: King Pedro is a variant of the popular American card game Pedro (also known as Cinch or 63), played primarily in the northeastern United States and Canada. It adds the King of trumps as an additional scoring card worth 5 points, making the total points available 19 per hand instead of the standard 14. It is a trick-taking game where the 5 of trumps (the Pedro) and the 5 of the same color (the Left Pedro) are the most valuable cards.

Developed from the 19th-century American game Pedro (also called Cinch or Double Pedro). The addition of the King as a scoring card was a regional variation that emerged in the northeastern United States and parts of Canada.
4 players in fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other.
Deal 9 cards to each player, 3 at a time. The turn to deal passes to the left after each hand.
